Anonymous, Gudrun, translated by Mary Pickering Nichols.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anonymous/gudrun/mary-pickering-nichols

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Anonymous, the author: no death year, because the work is anonymous.
- Mary Pickering Nichols, the translator, word-for-word translator and writer of the introduction or preface, died 1915 (Wikidata Q26179065, P570 1915-02-03).

First publication of the text used: 1889, the English translation by Mary Pickering Nichols. The country of first publication is not stated in the facts; the rule below does not need it. The Middle High German original was written circa 1250. (SE colophon: 'Gudrun was written circa 1250. It was translated from Middle High German in 1889 by Mary Pickering Nichols.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1889, before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier (Mary Pickering Nichols, the translator, died 1915), so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The country of first publication does not matter. The original is an anonymous work written circa 1250, before 1800, so it is public domain in every country whatever its country of origin.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/anonymous/gudrun/mary-pickering-nichols): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q26179065 (Mary Pickering Nichols), P570 1915-02-03.
